body: Did a bit more testing- it seems like enabling Slide on Slope resolves the problem in Godot phyics but not Jolt physics, so it might not be as simple as the SeperationRayShape3D being applied 'late'. May be related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100890 or https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/72090

`move_and_collide` consists of three stages:

1. Depenetration/recovery out of any current overlap
2. Shape-casting along the motion vector, from the depenetrated position
3. Final collision check where the shape-cast hit

I don't know why this was never documented, nor frankly why it was done this way to begin with, but when `slide_on_slope` is disabled it will not take part in that second stage, which means you're only ever getting the depenetration part of it, which is why you're seeing this clipping.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2dd26a027a99633231184616d4dd287bbdd1c0a3/modules/godot_physics_3d/godot_space_3d.cpp#L818-L825

The reason for the discrepancy between Jolt and Godot Physics, when enabling `slide_on_slope`, seems to be related to the floor being a `ConcavePolygonShape3D` and the fact that your `SeparationRayShape3D` is perfectly positioned at the edge between the two triangles. If you change the floor to be a convex shape (like a `BoxShape3D`) or if you just move the "character" slightly in either axis, you'll find that it works as expected with Jolt as well.

I suspect this discrepancy is effectively the same issue as #107900, meaning the only real fix is to either change your floor to not be a `ConcavePolygonShape3D`, and instead be a single convex shape, or to add one or more additional `SeparationRayShape3D` shapes to your character, in order to mitigate the precision errors that can arise from just a single ray-cast.

I see, thank you. Unfortunately using non-ConcavePolygonShape3D collision isn't really an option for level geometry. Hopefully https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/107900 is resolved, but even if it's not it would be nice if there was a way to have it participate normally in the 2nd stage of move_and_collide while not depending on normals for how the collision is actually resolved, like it does when slide_on_slope is disabled. I've already been working on a custom build so I'll try seeing if I can find a solution that way.

can't figure out where the separation ray separation is actually applied unfortunately. unless it just uses the normal system and doesn't have a "special case" anywhere?
also just found out for some reason even internal engine code uses dictionaries to pass data???? why????

> Unfortunately using non-ConcavePolygonShape3D collision isn't really an option for level geometry. Hopefully #107900 is resolved

I wouldn't bet on #107900 being resolved anytime soon. Your best bet is most likely to add one or more additional `SeparationRayShape3D`. You can have them be spaced apart very tightly and you'll still get the added stability.

> but even if it's not it would be nice if there was a way to have it participate normally in the 2nd stage of move_and_collide while not depending on normals for how the collision is actually resolved

I am a bit tempted to just remove that code I linked above, and the equivalent code in the Jolt Physics module. I struggle to see why `move_and_collide`/`move_and_slide` should behave differently when toggling `slide_on_slope`, outside of the documented change to the collision normal.

I could be missing some niche use-case though.

> can't figure out where the separation ray separation is actually applied unfortunately

The undesirable behavior is a result of the shape being filtered out during `move_and_collide` (or rather `body_test_motion` which powers it), which is the code I linked above. If you remove those lines you'll get the behavior you expect (in Godot Physics). The equivalent code to remove for Jolt would be this method:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b50ea8adec073c891763f7c8c2844bf207cf103/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_motion_filter_3d.cpp#L100-L113

Just change that method to always and unconditionally return `true`, and the `SeparationRayShape3D` won't be filtered out from the shape-cast stage anymore.

The changing of the normal happens elsewhere, but isn't relevant here.

> also just found out for some reason even internal engine code uses dictionaries to pass data???? why????

If by "internal engine code" you mean `JoltSeparationRayShape3D::set_data`, then it isn't internal per se. It's just a specialized handler for `PhysicsServer3D.shape_set_data`, which is a public script API.

@mihe A bit late but just realised - [#107900](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/107900) does not explain the discrepancy between Godot and Jolt physics. 107900 doesn't involve rays 'slipping through' cracks, it involves the normals returned. Specifically, the issue is that it gets face normals at the collision point without accounting for the direction the ray came from, which can lead to odd results when the same point is on the edge of multiple faces with _different normals_. That isn't the case here- it's a flat quad. This is a seperate issue.

Right, yeah, I guess the issue itself being resolved wouldn't actually do anything to help with this issue. The part of it I had in mind when linking it was [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/107900#issuecomment-3006015556) by the author of Jolt:

> Ray casts are infinitely thin, so it's very easy for rays to pass through cracks (e.g. due to float precision errors) and cause odd results.

So it seems to be a known shortcoming. It doesn't immediately explain why Godot Physics doesn't present this problem in the MRP, but given how fickle floating-point errors can be I also wouldn't expect the two engines to present these kinds of problems under the exact same circumstances.
